title.zh: 卷五十一 吳書六 宗室傳
title.en: Volume 51: Book of Wu 6 - Biographies of nobles
title.raw: 卷五十一 吳書六 宗室傳 Volume 51: Book of Wu 6 - Biographies of nobles

sentences.zh: 孫靜字幼臺，堅季弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Jing, courtesy name You'ai, was the youngest younger brother of Sun Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jing, styled You'ai, was Sun Jian's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 堅始舉事，靜糾合鄉曲及宗室五六百人以為保障，眾咸附焉。

translations.literal: When Jian first raised troops, Jing rallied several hundred men from the countryside and the lineage as a protective force—all adhered to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian first rebelled, Sun Jing raised five or six hundred local clansmen to shield him—and everyone rallied.

sentences.zh: 策破劉繇，定諸縣。

translations.literal: Ce defeated Liu Yao and pacified the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce defeated Liu Yao and brought the counties to heel.

sentences.zh: 進攻會稽，遣人請靜，靜將家屬與策會於錢唐。

translations.literal: Advancing against Kuaiji, he sent for Jing—Jing brought his household and met Ce at Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Kuaiji, Sun Ce summoned Sun Jing; Sun Jing brought his family and joined him at Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 是時太守王朗拒策於固陵，策數渡水戰，不能克。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Administrator Wang Lang held Ce off at Guling—Ce several times crossed the water to fight and could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang barred Guling; Sun Ce assailed the crossing again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 靜說策曰："朗負阻城守，難可卒拔。

translations.literal: Jing advised Ce, saying, "Lang relies on natural barriers and defends the city—he cannot be taken in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jing counseled, "Wang Lang is entrenched; a frontal storm will not break him quickly.

sentences.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，

translations.literal: Zha Brook lies several tens of li south of here
translations.idiomatic: Zha Ford lies dozens of li to the south—

sentences.zh: 〈查音祖加反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Phonetic gloss: Zha is read zu-jia fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pronunciation note: the place-name graph Zha reads zu-jia fan.

sentences.zh: 而道之要徑也，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備、出其不意者也。

translations.literal: and the road is a critical byway—it is fit to occupy that interior from there—what is called strike where he is unprepared, appear where he does not expect.
translations.idiomatic: —and the path is the back door. Seize it and you hit him unawares—exactly "attack where there is no readiness."

sentences.zh: 吾當自帥眾為軍前隊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: I shall personally lead the host as the army's vanguard—we are certain to break him.
translations.idiomatic: I will spearhead the assault myself—we will crack him open.

sentences.zh: "策曰："善。

translations.literal: Ce said, "Good.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce agreed.

sentences.zh: "乃詐令軍中曰："頃連雨水濁，兵飲之多腹痛，令促具罌缶數百口澄水。

translations.literal: Thereupon he falsely ordered the army, saying, "Recently continuous rain has muddied the water—soldiers drinking it suffer bellyaches—order them quickly to prepare several hundred jars and pots to settle the water.
translations.idiomatic: He spread a false order: the river water was foul from rain and sickened the men—every unit must fetch hundreds of jars to strain it clear.

sentences.zh: "至昏暮，羅以然火誑朗，便分軍夜投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。

translations.literal: At dusk he spread watchfires to deceive Lang, then divided the army by night to march the Zha Brook road and raid the camp at Gaoqian.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk decoy fires fooled Wang Lang; Sun Ce split his force and stole up Zha Ford by night to storm Gaoqian camp.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：今永兴县有高迁桥。〉

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi notes: Present-day Yongxing county has Gaoqian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Gaoqian Bridge still stands in Yongxing county.

sentences.zh: 朗大驚。

translations.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang panicked.

sentences.zh: 遣故丹楊太守周昕等帥兵前戰。

translations.literal: He dispatched former Grand Administrator of Danyang Zhou Xin and others to lead troops to fight in front.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the former Danyang grand administrator Zhou Xin and others to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 策破昕等，斬之，遂定會稽。

translations.literal: Ce defeated Xin and the others, beheaded them, and thereupon pacified Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce routed them, struck off Zhou Xin's head, and secured Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昕字大明。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji Records states: Xin's courtesy name was Daming.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji Records gives Zhou Xin the style Daming.

sentences.zh: 少游京师，师事太傅陈蕃，博览群书，明於风角，善推灾异。

translations.literal: In youth he traveled to the capital and studied under Grand Tutor Chen Fan, broadly reading many texts—skilled in wind-angle divination and good at inferring omens of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in Luoyang under Chen Fan, read widely, and mastered wind-angle lore and portents.

sentences.zh: 辟太尉府，举高第，稍迁丹杨太守。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Grand Commandant's office, recommended in high rank, gradually promoted to Grand Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the Grand Commandant's staff, advanced by recommendation, he rose to grand administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 曹公起义兵，昕前后遣兵万餘人助公征伐。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao raised loyal troops, Xin before and after dispatched more than ten thousand soldiers to assist the duke in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao raised his army, Zhou Xin sent him well over ten thousand men across several levies.

sentences.zh: 袁术之在淮南也，昕恶其淫虐，绝不与通。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shu was in Huainan, Xin detested his debauchery and cruelty and broke off all communication.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xin loathed Yuan Shu's cruelty in Huainan and cut ties.

sentences.zh: 献帝春秋曰：袁术遣吴景攻昕，未拔，景乃募百姓敢从周昕者死不赦。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu dispatched Wu Jing to attack Xin—unable to take him—Jing then recruited commoners, proclaiming death to any who followed Zhou Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian says Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing against Zhou Xin; failing, Wu Jing threatened death for anyone siding with Zhou.

sentences.zh: 昕曰：“我则不德，百姓何罪？

translations.literal: Xin said, "If I lack virtue, what crime have the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xin replied, "If I am unworthy, what fault lies with the people?

sentences.zh: ”遂散兵，还本郡。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispersed his troops and returned to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He disbanded his army and went home.

sentences.zh: 表拜靜為奮武校尉，欲授之重任，靜戀墳墓宗族，不樂出仕，求留鎮守。

translations.literal: Sun Ce memorialized and appointed Jing Colonel Who Rouses Might, wishing to entrust him heavy duty—Jing yearned for ancestral graves and lineage kinsmen, did not relish leaving office, and begged to remain as guardian defender.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce recommended Sun Jing as Colonel Who Rouses Might for greater responsibility; Sun Jing preferred to stay among tombs and kin, declined wider office, and asked to hold the homeland.

sentences.zh: 策從之。

translations.literal: Ce granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce agreed.

sentences.zh: 權統事，就遷昭義中郎將，終於家。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed governance, Jing was promoted on site to General of the Household Who Manifests Righteousness and ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Quan he rose to General of the Household for Manifesting Righteousness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有五子，皓、瑜、皎、奐、謙。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.

sentences.zh: 皓三子：綽、超、恭。

translations.literal: Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao fathered Chuo, Chao, and Gong.

sentences.zh: 超為偏將軍。

translations.literal: Chao served as Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chao became a lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 恭生峻。

translations.literal: Gong fathered Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gong was father to Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 綽生綝。

translations.literal: Chuo fathered Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo was father to Sun Lin.

sentences.zh: 靜次子瑜

translations.literal: Jing's second son Yu
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jing's second son: Yu

sentences.zh: 瑜字仲異，以恭義校尉始領兵眾。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zhongyi, first as Colonel Who Honors Righteousness began to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu, styled Zhongyi, first took command as Colonel Who Honors Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 是時賓客諸將多江西人，瑜虛心綏撫，得其歡心。

translations.literal: At that time guests and generals were mostly men west of the Yangzi—Yu with empty mind soothed and comforted them, winning their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his officers came from Jiangxi; Sun Yu treated them with open patience and won their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建安九年，領丹楊太守，為眾所附，至萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jian'an he became Grand Administrator of Danyang—men attached themselves to him until they exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 204 he became grand administrator of Danyang and drew more than ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 加綏遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與周瑜共討麻、保二屯，破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year together with Zhou Yu he campaigned against the Ma and Bao stockades and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 206 he joined Zhou Yu against the Ma and Bao camps and broke them.

sentences.zh: 後從權拒曹公於濡須，權欲交戰，瑜說權持重，權不從，軍果無功。

translations.literal: Later following Quan he resisted Duke Cao at Ruxu—Quan wished to give battle—Yu urged Quan to hold steady—Quan did not follow—the army indeed achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Ruxu against Cao Cao, Sun Quan wanted to fight; Sun Yu urged caution—Sun Quan ignored him and won nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷奮威將軍，領郡如故，自溧陽徙屯牛渚。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Displays Might, continuing to hold the commandery as before, transferring encampment from Liyang to Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to General Who Displays Might, he kept Danyang but moved his base from Liyang to Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 瑜以永安人饒助為襄安長，無錫人顏連為居巢長，使招納廬江二郡，各得降附。

translations.literal: Yu appointed Rao Zhu of Yong'an as magistrate of Xiang'an and Yan Lian of Wuxi as magistrate of Juchao and sent them to recruit and admit Lujiang's two commanderies—each obtained surrender and attachment.
translations.idiomatic: He named Rao Zhu of Yong'an over Xiang'an and Yan Lian of Wuxi over Juchao to draw Lujiang's two commanderies—both yielded.

sentences.zh: 濟陰人馬普篤學好古，瑜厚禮之，使二府將吏子弟數百人就受業，遂立學官，臨饗講肄。

translations.literal: Ma Pu of Jiyin was devoted to learning and honored antiquity—Yu treated him with generous ritual and had several hundred sons of generals and clerks of the two offices go to receive instruction—thereupon he established a school office—personally presiding he lectured and drilled.
translations.idiomatic: The scholar Ma Pu of Jiyin won Sun Yu's patronage; hundreds of officers' sons studied under him until Sun Yu founded a school and lectured in person.

sentences.zh: 是時諸將皆以軍務為事，而瑜好樂墳典，雖在戎旅，誦聲不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the generals all took military affairs as their business—yet Yu delighted in the Classics and histories—even amid camp life his recitation never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: While other generals lived for war, Sun Yu buried himself in the Classics—even on campaign he chanted texts without cease.

sentences.zh: 年三十九，建安二十年卒。

translations.literal: At thirty-nine years he died in the twentieth year of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine in Jian'an 215.

sentences.zh: 瑜五子：彌、熙、耀、曼、紘。

translations.literal: Yu had five sons: Mi, Xi, Yao, Man, and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Mi, Xi, Yao, Man, and Hong.

sentences.zh: 曼至將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: Man reached general rank and was enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Man rose to general and received a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 孫皎字叔朗，始拜護軍校尉，領眾二千餘人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiao, courtesy name Shulang, was first appointed Colonel Who Guards the Army and commanded more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiao, styled Shulang, began as Colonel Who Guards the Army with over two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是時曹公數出濡須，皎每赴拒，號為精銳。

translations.literal: At that time Duke Cao repeatedly emerged at Ruxu—Jiao each time went to resist and was titled crack elite.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cao Cao probed Ruxu, Sun Jiao countered—his corps was reckoned elite.

sentences.zh: 遷都護征虜將軍，代程普督夏口。

translations.literal: He was promoted Chief Controller General Who Subdues Captives, replacing Cheng Pu as supervisor of Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chief Controller and General Who Subdues Captives, succeeding Cheng Pu at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 黃蓋及兄瑜卒，又並其軍。

translations.literal: When Huang Gai and elder brother Yu died, he also annexed their armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Gai and Sun Yu died, he absorbed their commands.

sentences.zh: 賜沙羨、雲杜、南新市、竟陵為奉邑。

translations.literal: He was granted Shaxian, Yundu, Nanxinshi, and Jingling as revenue estates.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan granted him Shaxian, Yundu, Nanxinshi, and Jingling as fiefs.

sentences.zh: 自置長吏。

translations.literal: He appointed senior officials himself.
translations.idiomatic: He chose his own magistrates for those lands.

sentences.zh: 輕財能施，善於交結，與諸葛瑾至厚。

translations.literal: He treated wealth lightly and could give generously—skilled at forming friendships—and was extremely thick with Zhuge Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Open-handed and sociable, he was closest to Zhuge Jin.

sentences.zh: 委廬江劉靖以得失，江夏李允以眾事，廣陵吳碩、河南張梁以軍旅，而傾心親待，莫不自盡。

translations.literal: He entrusted Liu Jing of Lujiang with assessing gains and losses—Li Yun of Jiangxia with miscellaneous affairs—Wu Shuo of Guangling and Zhang Liang of Henan with military affairs—and leaned on them with intimate favor—none failed to give their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He delegated strategy to Liu Jing of Lujiang, administration to Li Yun of Jiangxia, and operations to Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang—each repaid his trust fully.

sentences.zh: 皎嘗遣兵候獲魏邊將吏美女以進皎，皎更其衣服送還之，下令曰："今所誅者曹氏，其百姓何罪?自今以往，不得擊其老弱。

translations.literal: Jiao once sent scouts who captured Wei frontier officers' beautiful women to present to Jiao—Jiao changed their clothing and sent them back—issuing an order saying, "What we now punish is the Cao clan—what crime have their common people? From this time forward you may not strike their old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: When scouts sent him captive Wei women, Sun Jiao reclothed them and returned them, decreeing that only Cao Cao's men were targets—not civilians, young or old.

sentences.zh: "由是江淮間多歸附者。

translations.literal: By this means many between the Yangzi and Huai attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hence many north of the river rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗以小故與甘寧忿爭，或以諫寧，寧曰："臣子一例，征虜雖公子，何可專行侮人邪!吾值明主，但當輸效力命，以報所天，誠不能隨俗屈典矣。

translations.literal: Once over a small matter he quarreled angrily with Gan Ning—some remonstrated with Ning—Ning said, "Minister and subject share one rule—though the General Who Subdues Captives is the lord's son—how can he exclusively insult others! I have encountered an enlightened lord—I ought only to devote strength and life to repay Heaven—I truly cannot bend ritual to vulgar ways!
translations.idiomatic: After a petty spat with Gan Ning, Gan Ning told mediators: "Ministers owe one duty—even a commander who is the ruler's cousin cannot bully men at will. I serve an enlightened lord—I owe my life to him—I will not swallow insult to save face!

sentences.zh: "權聞之，以書讓皎曰：

translations.literal: When Quan heard of it, he wrote reproaching Jiao, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wrote Sun Jiao a sharp rebuke:

sentences.zh: 自吾與北方為敵，中間十年，初時相持年小，今者且三十矣。

translations.literal: Since I and the north have been foes—in the middle ten years—at first when we faced each other we were still young—now some approach thirty.
translations.idiomatic: We have faced the north ten years; we were boys when this began—now some of us near thirty.

sentences.zh: 孔子言‘三十而立’，非但謂五經也。

translations.literal: Confucius spoke of "standing firm at thirty"—not only referring to the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said one stands firm at thirty—meaning maturity of character, not mere book learning.

sentences.zh: 授卿以精兵，委卿以大任，都護諸將於千里之外，欲使如楚任昭奚恤，揚威於北境。

translations.literal: I entrusted you with crack troops—delegated you great duty—chief controller of generals a thousand li away—wishing to make you like Chu's employment of Zhao Xixu—displaying might on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I gave you elite troops and far-reaching command—like Chu's Zhao Xixu—to awe the northern border.

sentences.zh: 非徒相使逞私志而已。

translations.literal: Not merely to let each other indulge private whims.
translations.idiomatic: Not so you could indulge private tempers.

sentences.zh: 近聞卿與甘興霸飲，因酒發作，侵陵其人，其人求屬呂蒙督中。

translations.literal: Recently I heard you drank with Gan Xingba—because of wine you erupted—bullying that man—that man sought to attach to Staff Supervisor Lu Meng's command.
translations.idiomatic: I hear wine unleashed you on Gan Ning—who then asked to serve under Lu Meng.

sentences.zh: 此人雖粗豪，有不如人意時，然其較略大丈夫也。

translations.literal: This man, though rough and bold—sometimes falls short of human expectation—yet in outline he is a great husband.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning is crude yet he is a man in full.

sentences.zh: 吾親之者，非私之也。

translations.literal: My treating him kindly is not private favor.
translations.idiomatic: My warmth toward him is not favoritism.

sentences.zh: 我親愛之，卿疏憎之。

translations.literal: I am intimate with him—you are distant and loathe him.
translations.idiomatic: I favor him while you spurn him.

sentences.zh: 卿所為每與吾違，其可久乎？

translations.literal: What you do constantly contravenes me—can this long endure?
translations.idiomatic: You defy me at every turn—how long can this last?

sentences.zh: 夫居敬而行簡，可以臨民；

translations.literal: Dwelling in reverence while acting with simplicity—by this one may oversee the people;
translations.idiomatic: Revere duty and keep actions plain—that rules people.

sentences.zh: 愛人多容，可以得眾。

translations.literal: Loving many and tolerating much—by this one can win the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Love broadly and forgive—that wins the host.

sentences.zh: 二者尚不能知，安可董督在遠，禦寇濟難乎？

translations.literal: If you cannot yet grasp these two—how can you oversee from afar—repelling enemies and bridging peril?
translations.idiomatic: If you miss both lessons, how will you command on a distant front?

sentences.zh: 卿行長大，特受重任，上有遠方瞻望之視，下有部曲朝夕從事，何可恣意有盛怒邪？

translations.literal: You have grown tall—specially receiving heavy responsibility—above there is the gaze of distant lands looking on—below there are personal troops attending morning and evening—how can you indulge wanton fits of rage?
translations.idiomatic: You are grown, heavily tasked—every eye watches—your men attend you daily—how dare you rage at will?

sentences.zh: 人誰無過，貴其能改，宜追前愆，深自咎責。

translations.literal: Who among men lacks fault—the precious thing is the ability to change—you ought to pursue former errors and deeply blame yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone errs—the virtue is to mend—own your fault fully.

sentences.zh: 今故煩諸葛子瑜重宣吾意。

translations.literal: Now I therefore trouble Zhuge Ziyu again to proclaim my intent.
translations.idiomatic: I send Zhuge Jin again to repeat my meaning.

sentences.zh: 臨書摧愴，心悲淚下。

translations.literal: Writing this letter I am crushed with sorrow—my heart grieves and tears fall.
translations.idiomatic: My hand shakes as I write—I weep over this.

sentences.zh: 皎得書，上疏陳謝，遂與寧結厚。

translations.literal: When Jiao received the letter he submitted a memorial expressing apology—thereupon he and Ning formed deep friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiao apologized by memorial and sealed firm friendship with Gan Ning.

sentences.zh: 後呂蒙當襲南郡，權欲令皎與蒙為左右部大督。

translations.literal: Later when Lu Meng was to raid Nan Commandery—Quan wished to make Jiao and Meng left and right chief commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Meng struck Nan Commandery, Sun Quan meant to pair him with Sun Jiao as dual commanders.

sentences.zh: 蒙說權曰："若至尊以征虜能，宜用之。

translations.literal: Meng urged Quan, saying, "If the Supreme One thinks the General Who Subdues Captives capable—employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Meng argued: "If you trust Sun Jiao—use him.

sentences.zh: 以蒙能，宜用蒙。

translations.literal: If Meng is capable—employ Meng.
translations.idiomatic: If you trust me—use me alone.

sentences.zh: 昔周瑜、程普為左右部督，共攻匯陵，雖事決於瑜，普自恃久將，且俱是督，遂共不睦，幾敗國事，此目前之戒也。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu were left and right chief commanders—together attacking Jiangling—although affairs were decided by Yu—Pu relied on being a veteran general—and both being commanders—thereupon together were not harmonious—almost ruining state affairs—this is the warning before our eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu once split command at Jiangling—Yu decided matters yet Cheng Pu, the veteran, quarreled—and nearly wrecked the campaign. Remember that lesson.

sentences.zh: "權寤，謝蒙曰："以卿為大督，命皎為後繼。

translations.literal: Quan understood—apologized to Meng saying, "I make you chief commander—I order Jiao as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan saw the point, thanked Lu Meng, and named him sole commander with Sun Jiao in reserve.

sentences.zh: "禽關羽，定荊州，皖有力焉。

translations.literal: Capturing Guan Yu—settling Jing Province—Jiao had strength therein.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiao bore his share in taking Guan Yu and securing Jing.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jian'an 219.

sentences.zh: 權追錄其功，封子胤為丹楊侯。

translations.literal: Quan posthumously recorded his merit—enfeoffing son Yin as Marquis of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ennobled his son Sun Yin marquis of Danyang for his father's deeds.

sentences.zh: 胤卒，無子。

translations.literal: Yin died—without sons.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yin died without heir.

sentences.zh: 弟晞嗣。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Sun Xi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 領兵，有罪自殺，國除。

translations.literal: He commanded troops—having guilt—committed suicide—the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xi led troops but disgraced himself and killed himself—the marquisate was struck.

sentences.zh: 弟咨、彌。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Zi and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers Sun Zi and Sun Mi.

sentences.zh: 儀皆將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: Zi and Mi both became generals—were enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zi and Sun Mi both rose to general and received marquisates.

sentences.zh: 咨羽林督，儀無難督。

translations.literal: Zi—Colonel of the Feathered Forest—Yi—Colonel Who Faces Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zi led the Feathered Forest guard; Sun Mi commanded the Unmatched Difficulty corps.

sentences.zh: 咨為滕胤所殺，儀為孫峻所害。

translations.literal: Zi was killed by Teng Yin—Yi was harmed by Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin killed Sun Zi; Sun Jun murdered Sun Mi.

sentences.zh: 孫奐字季明。

translations.literal: Sun Huan, courtesy name Jiming.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan, styled Jiming.

sentences.zh: 兄皎既卒，代統其眾，以揚武中郎將領江夏太守。

translations.literal: When elder brother Jiao had died—he replaced him in commanding his host—as General of the Household Who Displays Might he held Grand Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jiao's death Sun Huan took his army as General of the Household Who Displays Might and grand administrator of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 在事一年，遵皎舊跡，禮劉靖、李允、吳碩、張梁及江夏閭舉等，並納其善。

translations.literal: In office one year—following Jiao's old tracks—he treated Liu Jing, Li Yun, Wu Shuo, Zhang Liang, and Lü Ju of Jiangxia with ritual—and adopted their good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: For a year he kept Sun Jiao's pattern—honoring Liu Jing, Li Yun, Wu Shuo, Zhang Liang, and Lü Ju—and heeded their advice.

sentences.zh: 奐訥於造次而敏於當宮，軍民稱之。

translations.literal: Huan was slow in hasty moments yet keen when holding office—soldiers and civilians praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Slow to rush yet sharp in office, he won soldiers and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 黃武五年，權攻石陽，奐以地主，使所部將軍鮮于丹帥五千人先斷淮道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangwu—Quan attacked Shiyang—Huan as local host ordered his subordinate General Xianyu Dan to lead five thousand men first to cut the Huai road.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 226 Sun Quan struck Shiyang; Sun Huan, the local commander, sent General Xianyu Dan with five thousand men to sever the Huai route first.

sentences.zh: 自帥吳碩、張梁五千人為軍前鋒，降高城，得三將。

translations.literal: Personally leading Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang with five thousand men as the army's van—he reduced Gaocheng—obtaining three generals.
translations.idiomatic: He led Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang's five thousand as vanguard, took Gaocheng, and captured three enemy generals.

sentences.zh: 大軍引還，權詔使在前住，駕過其軍，見奐軍陳整齊，權歎曰："初吾憂其遲鈍，今治軍，諸將少能及者，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: The great army withdrew—Quan ordered him to halt in front—the imperial carriage passed his army—seeing Huan's army formation orderly—Quan sighed and said, "At first I worried he was dull—now governing the army—few generals can match him—I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: When the army pulled back Sun Quan rode past Sun Huan's ranks—saw perfect order—and sighed, "I feared him slow—yet few command so well—I need not worry now.

sentences.zh: "拜揚威將軍，封沙羨侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Displays Might—enfeoffed Marquis of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him General Who Displays Might and marquis of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 吳碩、張梁皆裨將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang were both Lieutenant Generals—granted noble rank Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shuo and Zhang Liang each became lieutenant general with marquis-within-the-passes rank.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：初权在武昌，欲还都建业，而虑水道溯流二千里，一旦有警，不相赴及，以此怀疑。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: At first when Quan was at Wuchang he wished to move the capital back to Jianye—yet worried that the water route upstream two thousand li—if alarm came suddenly—would not allow mutual rescue—by this he harbored doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Quan at Wuchang hesitated to return the court to Jianye—a two-thousand-li upstream haul might isolate him if crisis struck.

sentences.zh: 及至夏口，於坞中大会百官议之，诏曰：“诸将吏勿拘位任，其有计者，为国言之。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiakou—within the dock he greatly assembled the hundred officials to deliberate—issuing an edict saying, "Generals and clerks—do not be constrained by rank—whoever has a plan—speak for the state.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiakou he convened his officers in the naval yard and ordered every rank to speak freely for the realm.

sentences.zh: ”诸将或陈宜立栅栅夏口，或言宜重设铁锁者，权皆以为非计。

translations.literal: Some generals urged it fit to erect palisades at Xiakou—or said it fit heavily to set iron chains—Quan deemed neither a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed palisades at Xiakou or iron boom chains—Sun Quan rejected both.

sentences.zh: 时梁为小将，未有知名，乃越席而进曰：“臣闻香饵引泉鱼，重币购勇士，今宜明树赏罚之信，遣将入沔，与敌争利，形势既成，彼不敢干也。

translations.literal: At that time Liang was a minor general—not yet known by reputation—thereupon crossed his mat and advanced saying, "Your subject has heard sweet bait lures fish in springs—heavy gold buys brave warriors—now it is fit clearly to plant faith in rewards and punishments—dispatch generals into the Mian—contend with the foe for advantage—once the situation is formed—they will not dare meddle.
translations.idiomatic: Minor officer Zhang Liang stepped forward: lure fighters with clear rewards, thrust into the Han River to seize the initiative, and the enemy will keep clear.

sentences.zh: 使武昌有精兵万人，付智略者任将，常使严整。

translations.literal: Cause Wuchang to have crack troops ten thousand men—entrust them to a commander of wisdom and strategy—constantly keep them strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Station ten thousand veterans at Wuchang under a proven strategist—always combat-ready.

sentences.zh: 一旦有警，应声相赴。

translations.literal: Once alarm comes—respond to sound and march to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Then reinforcements can answer any alarm at once.

sentences.zh: 作甘水城，轻舰数千，诸所宜用，皆使备具。

translations.literal: Build Ganshui city—light warcraft several thousand—whatever ought be used—cause all to be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Build Ganshui fortress, ready thousands of light craft—every contingency covered.

sentences.zh: 如此开门延敌，敌自不来矣。

translations.literal: Thus opening the gate to invite the enemy—the enemy of themselves will not come.
translations.idiomatic: Show strength openly and the foe will not dare approach.

sentences.zh: ”权以梁计为最得，即超增梁位。

translations.literal: Quan deemed Liang's plan the most fitting—immediately promoted Liang's rank beyond ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan adopted Zhang Liang's plan and jumped him in rank.

sentences.zh: 后稍以功进至沔中督。〉

translations.literal: Later gradually by merit he advanced to inspector within the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by merit to command the Middle Han defenses.

sentences.zh: 奐亦愛樂儒生，覆命部曲子弟就業，後仕進朝廷者數十人。

translations.literal: Huan also loved and delighted in scholars—again ordered personal troops' sons and younger brothers to attend studies—later those who entered office at court numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan too cherished scholars—sent his officers' sons to school—and dozens later served at court.

sentences.zh: 年四十，嘉禾三年卒。

translations.literal: At forty years he died in the third year of Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty in Jiahe 234.

sentences.zh: 子承嗣，以昭武中郎將代統兵，領郡。

translations.literal: Son Cheng succeeded—as General of the Household Who Displays Might he replaced command of troops—holding the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Cheng inherited his command as General of the Household Who Displays Might and kept Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 赤烏六年卒，無子，封承庶弟壹奉奐後，襲業為將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chiwu he died—without sons—the fief named Cheng's younger brother by a concubine Yi to continue Huan's line—succeeding the enterprise as general.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng died childless in Chiwu 243; Sun Yi, a younger half-brother, inherited to continue Sun Huan's line.

sentences.zh: 孫峻之誅諸葛恪也，壹與全熙、施績攻恪弟公安督融，融自殺。

translations.literal: When Sun Jun executed Zhuge Ke—Yi together with Quan Xi and Shi Ji attacked Ke's younger brother Public Security supervisor Rong—Rong committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jun slew Zhuge Ke, Sun Yi joined Quan Xi and Shi Ji against Zhuge Rong at Gongan—Rong killed himself.

sentences.zh: 壹從鎮南遷鎮軍，假節督夏口。

translations.literal: Yi followed promotion from Defends the South to Stabilizes the Army—borrowed insignia—supervised Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi rose from Defends the South general to Stabilizes the Army with ceremonial axe and Xiakou command.

sentences.zh: 及孫綝誅滕胤、呂據，據、胤皆壹皆之妹夫也，壹弟封又知胤、據謀，自殺。

translations.literal: When Sun Lin executed Teng Yin and Lu Ju—Ju and Yin were both Yi's brothers-in-law—Yi's younger brother Feng also knew Yin's and Ju's plot—and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Lin killed Teng Yin and Lu Ju—both men had married Sun Yi's sisters—his brother Feng, privy to their plot, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 綝遣朱異潛襲壹。

translations.literal: Lin dispatched Zhu Yi to secretly raid Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin sent Zhu Yi to ambush Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 異至武昌，壹知其攻己，率部曲千餘口過將胤妻奔魏。

translations.literal: When Yi reached Wuchang—Yi knew they attacked him—led personal troops more than a thousand households crossing—escorting Yin's wife fleeing to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi learned at Wuchang that Sun Lin meant to strike—he fled north with over a thousand dependents and Teng Yin's wife.

sentences.zh: 魏以壹為車騎將軍、儀同三司，封吳侯，以故主芳貴人邢氏妻子。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Yi General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity of the Three Ducal Ministers—enfeoffed Marquis of Wu—and gave him in marriage the Lady Xing—honored consort of former Wei emperor Fang—with wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made him chariot-and-cavalry general with Three Excellencies honors, marquis of Wu, and married him to Lady Xing—once honored consort of Emperor Cao Fang—along with her household.

sentences.zh: 邢美色妒忌，下不堪命，遂共殺壹及邢氏。

translations.literal: Xing's beauty incited jealousy—those below could not endure her commands—thereupon together they killed Yi and Lady Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xing's jealousy drove her servants past endurance—they murdered Sun Yi and her.

sentences.zh: 壹入魏

translations.literal: Yi entered Wei
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: （黃初）

translations.literal: (Huangchu era)
translations.idiomatic: The incident fell in the Wei Huangchu period.

sentences.zh: 三年死。

translations.literal: in the third year died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 孫賁字伯陽；

translations.literal: Sun Fen zi Boyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen, styled Boyang—

sentences.zh: 父羌字聖

translations.literal: Father Qiang zi Sheng
translations.idiomatic: his father Sun Qiang, styled Sheng

translations.literal: (Yi)
translations.idiomatic: (variant reading Yi)

sentences.zh: ，堅同產兄也，賁早失二親，弟輔嬰孩，賁自贍育，友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: —was full younger brother by the same birth as Jian—Fen early lost both parents—younger brother Fu an infant—Fen himself supported and raised him—friendship and love were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: —was Sun Jian's full brother. Orphaned young with infant brother Sun Fu, Sun Fen raised him—bonded in deepest affection.

sentences.zh: 為郡督郵守長。

translations.literal: He served as commandery Recording Officer and defender chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recording officer and acting county chief.

sentences.zh: 堅於長沙舉義兵，賁去吏從征伐。

translations.literal: When Jian raised righteous troops at Changsha—Fen left office to follow in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian rose at Changsha, Sun Fen resigned to join him.

sentences.zh: 堅薨，賁攝帥餘眾，扶送靈柩。

translations.literal: When Jian passed away—Fen acting commanded the remaining host—escorting the funeral bier.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian died Sun Fen led the remnant army and bore the coffin.

sentences.zh: 後袁術徙壽春，賁又依之。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Shu moved to Shouchun—Fen again relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Fen followed Yuan Shu to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 術從兄紹用會稽周昂為九江太守，紹與術不協，術遣賁攻破昂於陰陵。

translations.literal: Shu's elder cousin Shao employed Zhou Ang of Kuaiji as Grand Administrator of Jiujiang—Shao and Shu were not harmonious—Shu dispatched Fen to defeat Ang at Yinling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had named Zhou Ang of Kuaiji over Jiujiang; at odds with Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu sent Sun Fen to crush Zhou Ang at Yinling.

sentences.zh: 術表賁領豫州刺史，轉丹楊都尉，行征虜將軍，討平山越。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized Fen acting Inspector of Yu Province—transferred Danyang Commandant—acting General Who Subdues Captives—campaigning to pacify the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu memorialized Sun Fen as inspector of Yu Province, then Danyang commandant and acting General Who Subdues Captives against the Yue hills.

sentences.zh: 為楊州刺史劉繇所迫逐，因將士眾還住歷陽。

translations.literal: Pressed and chased by Inspector of Yang Province Liu Yao—thereupon leading officers and troops returned to encamp at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Harried by Liu Yao, he withdrew to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，術復使賁與吳景共擊樊能、張英等，未能拔。

translations.literal: Before long Shu again ordered Fen together with Wu Jing jointly to strike Fan Neng, Zhang Ying, and others—unable to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Shu paired him with Wu Jing against Fan Neng and Zhang Ying—without success.

sentences.zh: 及策東渡，助賁、景破英、能等，遂進擊劉繇。

translations.literal: When Ce crossed east—helped Fen and Jing defeat Ying, Neng, and others—thereupon advanced to strike Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce crossed the river and with Sun Fen and Wu Jing broke Fan Neng and Zhang Ying, then turned on Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 繇走豫章。

translations.literal: Yao fled to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao fled toward Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 策遣賁、景還壽春報術，值術僭號，署置百官。

translations.literal: Ce dispatched Fen and Jing to return to Shouchun to report to Shu—happening on Shu's usurped title—setting up the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent them back to Shouchun—into Yuan Shu's sham court.

sentences.zh: 除賁九江太守。

translations.literal: He appointed Fen Grand Administrator of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu named Sun Fen grand administrator of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 賁不就，棄妻孥還江南。

translations.literal: Fen did not take up post—abandoning wife and children returned south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen refused the post and slipped home to the south shore without his family.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：袁术以吴景守广陵，策族兄香亦为术所用，作汝南太守，而令贲为将军，领兵在寿春。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Yuan Shu had Wu Jing defend Guangling—Ce's lineage elder brother Xiang was also employed by Shu—made Grand Administrator of Runan—and ordered Fen as general commanding troops at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan adds that Yuan Shu stationed Wu Jing at Guangling and employed cousin Sun Xiang as Runan administrator while Sun Fen led troops at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 策与景等书曰：“今征江东，未知二三君意云何耳？

translations.literal: Ce wrote Jing and others saying, "Now campaigning east of the Yangzi—I do not know what intent you several gentlemen hold?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce wrote Wu Jing: "I march east—will you stand with me?

sentences.zh: ”景即弃守归，贲困而后免，香以道远独不得还。

translations.literal: Jing immediately abandoned defense and returned—Fen was trapped afterward freed—Xiang because the road was distant alone could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing came over at once; Sun Fen escaped Yuan Shu's grip; Sun Xiang stayed stranded far away.

sentences.zh: 吴书曰：香字文阳。

translations.literal: The Wu Book states: Xiang's courtesy name was Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Book styles Sun Xiang Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 父孺，字仲孺，坚再从弟也，仕郡主簿功曹。

translations.literal: Father Ru—courtesy name Zhongru—was Jian's second cousin once removed—served the commandery as chief clerk and merit assessor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Ru, styled Zhongru—Sun Jian's second cousin—served as chief clerk and merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 香从坚征伐有功，拜郎中。

translations.literal: Xiang followed Jian in campaigns with merit—appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiang campaigned with Sun Jian and became a Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 后为袁术驱驰，加征南将军，死於寿春。〉

translations.literal: Later for Yuan Shu he drove hard—advanced General Who Defends the South—died at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He later ran errands for Yuan Shu as General Who Defends the South and died at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 時策已平吳、會二郡，賁與策征廬江太守劉勳、江夏太守黃祖，軍旋，聞繇病死，過定豫章，上賁領太守，

translations.literal: At that time Ce had already pacified Wu and Kuaiji two commanderies—Fen together with Ce campaigned against Grand Administrator of Lujiang Liu Xun and Grand Administrator of Jiangxia Huang Zu—army returning—hearing Yao died of illness—passing settled Yuzhang—memorialized Fen acting Grand Administrator
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu and Kuaiji were his, Sun Ce took Sun Fen against Liu Xun and Huang Zu; returning after Liu Yao's death, he secured Yuzhang and named Sun Fen acting grand administrator

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：时丹杨僮芝自署庐陵太守，策留贲弟辅领兵住南昌，策谓贲曰：“兄今据豫章，是扼僮芝咽喉而守其门户矣。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: At that time Tong Zhi of Danyang had styled himself Grand Administrator of Luling—Ce retained Fen's younger brother Fu commanding troops stationed at Nanchang—Ce said to Fen, "Elder brother now holds Yuzhang—this is choking Tong Zhi's throat while guarding his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan quotes Sun Ce: with Tong Zhi holding Luling illegally, Sun Fu garrisoned Nanchang—"You throttle Tong Zhi's throat from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 但当伺其形便，因令国仪杖兵而进，使公瑾为作势援，一举可定也。

translations.literal: Only ought watch for his posture's convenience—thereby order Guoyi to lead arms and advance—cause Gongjin to make threatening support—one stroke can settle it.
translations.idiomatic: Wait for his slip, send Sun Guoyi forward under Zhou Yu's covering feint—one blow finishes it.

sentences.zh: ”后贲闻芝病，即如策计。

translations.literal: Later Fen heard Zhi fell ill—immediately according to Ce's plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Zhi fell ill Sun Fen acted on that plan.

sentences.zh: 周瑜到巴兵，辅遂得进据庐陵。〉

translations.literal: When Zhou Yu reached Baqiu—Fu thereupon was able to advance and occupy Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou Yu joined the advance at Baqiu, Sun Fu took Luling.

sentences.zh: 後封都亭侯。

translations.literal: Later enfeoffed Marquis of Du Village.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Fen became marquis of Du village.

sentences.zh: 建安十三年，使者劉隱奉詔拜賁為征虜將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an envoy Liu Yin bearing edict appointed Fen General Who Subdues Captives—holding commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 208 an envoy invested him as General Who Subdues Captives while he kept Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 在官十一年卒。

translations.literal: In office eleven years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after eleven years in office.

sentences.zh: 子鄰嗣。

translations.literal: Son Lin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Lin inherited.

sentences.zh: 鄰年九歲，代領豫章，近封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Lin at nine years replaced holding Yuzhang—soon enfeoffed Marquis of Douxiang Village.
translations.idiomatic: At nine Sun Lin succeeded in Yuzhang and soon held a Douxiang village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：邻字公达，雅性精敏，幼有令誉。〉

translations.literal: The Wu Book states: Lin's courtesy name Gongda—by nature refined and keen—youth had fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Book calls him Gongda—acute from boyhood with a shining name.

sentences.zh: 在郡垂二十年，討平叛賊，功績修理。

translations.literal: In the commandery nearly twenty years—campaigning to pacify rebel bandits—merit records orderly.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he crushed rebels and kept sound registers.

sentences.zh: 召還武昌，為繞帳督。

translations.literal: Summoned back to Wuchang—became Cord Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Wuchang as cord encampment commander.

sentences.zh: 時太常潘浚掌荊州事，重安長陳留舒燮有罪下獄，浚嘗失燮，欲置之於法。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun oversaw Jing Province affairs—Zhong'an chief Shu Xie of Chenliu had guilt—entered prison—Jun once lost Xie—wished to place him under law.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Jun governed Jingzhou; Shu Xie of Chenliu, magistrate of Zhong'an, was jailed—Pan Jun, nursing an old slight, meant to punish him harshly.

sentences.zh: 論者多為有言，浚猶不釋。

translations.literal: Debators many spoke for him—Jun still did not release.
translations.idiomatic: Many pleaded for Shu Xie—Pan Jun would not relent.

sentences.zh: 鄰謂浚曰："舒伯膺兄弟爭死，海內義之，以為美談，仲膺又奉國舊意。

translations.literal: Lin said to Jun, "Shu Boying's brothers contended to die—within the seas praised them—deemed it fine discourse—Zhongying moreover upholds the state's former intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin warned Pan Jun: "The Shu brothers once vied to die for each other—the empire sang of it—Shu Xie still honors that loyal house.

sentences.zh: 今君殺其子弟，若天下一統，青蓋北巡，中州士人必問仲膺繼嗣，答者雲潘承明殺燮，於事何如?"浚意即解，燮用得濟。

translations.literal: Now you kill his sons and younger brothers—if All-under-Heaven unifies—the green canopy tours north—Central Plain scholars will surely ask Zhongying's heir—respondents will say Pan Chengming killed Xie—toward the affair how?
translations.idiomatic: Kill his kin now and when the Jin someday reunites the north, educated men will ask who slew Shu Xie—will you answer that Pan Jun murdered him?

sentences.zh: 〈《博物志》曰：仲膺名邵。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Natural Matters states: Zhongying's name was Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Curiosities names him Shu Shao.

sentences.zh: 初，伯膺亲友为人所杀，仲膺为报怨。

translations.literal: At first Boying's kin and friends were killed by someone—Zhongying avenged the grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu Boying's kin were murdered; Shu Shao avenged them.

sentences.zh: 事觉，兄弟争死，皆得免。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed—brothers contended to die—both obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Caught, both brothers demanded execution—the court spared both.

sentences.zh: 袁术时，邵为阜陵长。

translations.literal: During Yuan Shu's time—Shao was chief of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan Shu, Shu Shao governed Fuling.

sentences.zh: 亦见江表传。〉

translations.literal: Also seen in Jiangbiao zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan tells the same tale.

sentences.zh: 鄰遷夏口沔中督、威遠將軍，所居任職。

translations.literal: Lin transferred Xiakou Han inspector—General Who Might Reaches Afar—where he dwelt in office competent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin moved to Han River inspector and General Who Might Reaches Afar—effective wherever posted.

sentences.zh: 赤烏十二年卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chiwu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chiwu 249.

sentences.zh: 子苗嗣。

translations.literal: Son Miao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Miao inherited.

sentences.zh: 苗弟旅及叔父安、熙、績，皆歷列位。

translations.literal: Miao's younger brother Lu and uncles An, Xi, and Ji—all held successive ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Sun Lu and uncles Sun An, Xi, and Ji all rose through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：邻又有子曰述，为武昌督，平荆州事。

translations.literal: The Wu Calendar states: Lin also had a son named Shu—was Wuchang inspector—pacifying Jing Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Calendar adds a son Shu—Wuchang inspector for Jing affairs.

sentences.zh: 震，无难督。

translations.literal: Zhen—Colonel Who Faces Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen led the Unmatched Difficulty corps.

sentences.zh: 谐，城门校尉。

translations.literal: Xie—Colonel of the Capital Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xie commanded the capital gates.

sentences.zh: 歆，乐乡督。

translations.literal: Xin—Lexiang inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xin held Lexiang command.

sentences.zh: 震后御晋军，与张悌俱死。

translations.literal: Zhen afterward opposed Jin troops—together with Zhang Ti died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen later fell fighting Jin beside Zhang Ti.

sentences.zh: 贲曾孙惠，字德施。

translations.literal: Fen's great-grandson Hui—courtesy name Deshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen's descendant Sun Hui, styled Deshi.

sentences.zh: 《惠别传》曰：惠好学有才智，晋永宁元年，赴齐王冏义，以功封晋兴侯，辟大司马贼曹属。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Hui states: Hui loved learning and had talent and wisdom—in the first year of Yongning of Jin—joined Prince of Qi's righteous army—by merit enfeoffed Marquis of Jinxing—summoned aide to Grand Marshal's Bandit Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His biography praises his scholarship—he followed Sima Jiong in Yongning 301, earned the Jinxing marquisate, and joined the Grand Marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 冏骄矜僭侈，天下失望。

translations.literal: Jiong was arrogant and extravagant beyond station—all under Heaven lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong grew arrogant—the realm despaired.

sentences.zh: 惠献言於冏，讽以五难、四不可，劝令委让万机，归籓青岱，辞甚深切。

translations.literal: Hui submitted words to Jiong—using indirect criticism through five difficulties and four impossibles—urging him to yield the myriad tasks—return to his fief at Qingdai—the rhetoric was very cutting and deep.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui memorialized five objections and four prohibitions—begging Jiong to surrender power and retire to his Qingdai fief—in blistering prose.

sentences.zh: 冏不能纳，顷之果败。

translations.literal: Jiong could not accept—before long indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong ignored him and soon fell.

sentences.zh: 成都王颖召为大将军参军。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying summoned him as Major to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying named him major on the grand general's staff.

sentences.zh: 是时颖将有事於长沙，以陆机为前锋都督。

translations.literal: At that time Ying had matters at Changsha—making Lu Ji van commander.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying then aimed at Changsha with Lu Ji as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 惠与机乡里亲厚，忧其致祸，谓之曰：“子盍让都督於王粹乎？

translations.literal: Hui and Ji were fellow villagers intimate and thick—worried he brought disaster—said to him, "Why not yield the van command to Wang Cui?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui, Lu Ji's townsman, urged him to yield command to Wang Cui.

sentences.zh: ”机曰：“将谓吾避贼首鼠，更速其害。

translations.literal: Ji said, "They will say I avoid the enemy—like a rat—more hastening its harm.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji refused: "They would call me a coward—and doom would come faster.

sentences.zh: ”机寻被戮，二弟云、耽亦见杀，惠甚伤恨之。

translations.literal: Ji soon was executed—two younger brothers Yun and Dan also were killed—Hui deeply wounded and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji died; brothers Lu Yun and Lu Dan followed—Sun Hui mourned bitterly.

sentences.zh: 永兴元年，乘舆幸鄴，司空东海王越治兵下邳，惠以书干越，诡其姓名，自称南岳逸民秦祕之，勉以勤王匡世之略，辞义甚美。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing—the imperial carriage favored Ye—Minister of Works Prince of Donghai Yue drilled troops at Xiapi—Hui by letter importuned Yue—using false name—calling himself South March Hermit Qin Mizhi—exhorting with doctrine of diligent royal house and aiding the age—the rhetoric and meaning very fine.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxing 304 Sun Hui wrote Prince Sima Yue at Xiapi under the alias Hermit Qin urging him to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 越省其书，榜题道衢，招求其人。

translations.literal: Yue examined his letter—posted its title on the road—summoned seeking that person.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue posted the essay on city gates seeking its author.

sentences.zh: 惠乃出见，越即以为记室参军，专掌文疏，豫参谋议。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon emerged to audience—Yue immediately made him secretary aide—solely managing documents—participating in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui revealed himself and became secretary—drafting strategy.

sentences.zh: 每造书檄，越或驿马催之，应命立成，皆有辞旨。

translations.literal: Whenever drafting letters and proclamations—Yue sometimes dispatched relay horses to hurry him—responding to command stood finished—all had rhetoric and purport.
translations.idiomatic: Relay riders rushed his prose—yet every draft landed polished.

sentences.zh: 累迁显职，后为广武将军、安丰内史。

translations.literal: Repeatedly transferred to prominent posts—later became General Who Extends Might—Administrator of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Extends Might and Anfeng administrator.

sentences.zh: 年四十七卒。

translations.literal: At forty-seven years died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 惠文翰凡数十首。〉

translations.literal: Hui's literary writings altogether several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to dozens of pieces.

sentences.zh: 孫輔字國儀，賁弟也，以揚武校尉佐孫策平三郡。

translations.literal: Sun Fu courtesy name Guoyi—Fen's younger brother—with Colonel Who Displays Might assisted Sun Ce pacifying three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, styled Guoyi—Sun Fen's brother—served Sun Ce as Colonel Who Displays Might across three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 策討丹楊七縣，使輔西屯歷陽以拒袁術，並招誘余民，鳩合遺散。

translations.literal: Ce campaigned against Danyang seven counties—ordered Fu west to encamp at Liyang to resist Yuan Shu—and recruit and entice remaining people—gather and unite scattered fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent him to Liyang to block Yuan Shu and rally refugees.

sentences.zh: 又從策討陵陽，生得祖郎等。

translations.literal: Again following Ce campaigned against Lingyang—captured alive Zu Lang and others.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Lingyang campaign and captured Zu Lang alive.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策既平定江东，逐袁胤。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce having pacified Jiangdong—expelled Yuan Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan continues: after Jiangdong fell, Sun Ce drove out Yuan Yin.

sentences.zh: 袁术深怨策，乃阴遣间使赍印绶与丹杨宗帅陵阳祖郎等，使激动山越，大合众，图共攻策。

translations.literal: Shu deeply resented Ce—thereupon secretly dispatched secret envoys bearing seals and ribbons to Danyang lineage chiefs Zuling Zu Lang and others—causing them to stir the mountain Yue—greatly combining hosts—plotting jointly to attack Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu hated Sun Ce and secretly sent seals to hill chiefs like Zu Lang of Luling, rousing the Yue to rise against him.

sentences.zh: 策自率将士讨郎，生获之。

translations.literal: Ce personally led officers and troops to campaign against Lang—capturing him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce led his army against Zu Lang and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 策谓郎曰：“尔昔袭击孤，斫孤马鞍，今创军立事，除弃宿恨，惟取能用，与天下通耳。

translations.literal: Ce said to Lang—"You formerly raided me—chopped my saddle—now raising an army and founding affairs—I discard old hatred—only taking those able for use—to communicate with All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: "You once ambushed me and hacked my saddle," Sun Ce said. "Now that I am building a realm I discard old grudges—I reward talent for the realm."

sentences.zh: 非但汝，汝莫恐怖。

translations.literal: Not only you—you must not fear.
translations.idiomatic: That holds for you too—do not be afraid."

sentences.zh: ”郎叩头谢罪。

translations.literal: Lang knocked his head apologizing for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Lang kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 即破械，赐衣服，署门下贼曹。

translations.literal: Immediately broke his fetters—bestowed clothing—appointed Gate Bandit Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce struck off his chains, gave him clothes, and named him bandit-clerk at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及军还，郎与太史慈俱在前导军，人以为荣。〉

translations.literal: When the army returned—Lang together with Taishi Ci both were in the van guard—people deemed it honor.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Zu Lang rode with Taishi Ci in the vanguard—a mark of honor."

sentences.zh: 策西襲廬江太守劉勳，輔隨從，身先士卒，有功。

translations.literal: Ce west raided Grand Administrator of Lujiang Liu Xun—Fu followed—body ahead of soldiers—with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu joined the western strike on Liu Xun of Lujiang, fighting in the van.

sentences.zh: 策立輔為廬陵太守，撫定屬城，分置長吏。

translations.literal: Ce established Fu as Grand Administrator of Luling—pacifying and settling dependent cities—dividing placement of senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce made him grand administrator of Luling, pacified its towns, and appointed magistrates.

sentences.zh: 遷平南將軍，假節領交州刺史。

translations.literal: Promoted General Who Pacifies the South—borrowed insignia—holding Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the South with ceremonial axe and the Jiaozhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 遣使與曹公相聞，事覺，權幽系之。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to communicate with Duke Cao—the affair was exposed—Quan imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: His secret messages to Cao Cao leaked; Sun Quan threw him in chains.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：辅恐权不能保守江东，因权出行东冶，乃遣人赍书呼曹公。

translations.literal: The Brief Model states—Fu feared Quan could not defend Jiangdong—because Quan traveled out to Dongye—thereupon dispatched men bearing letters summoning Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlue says Sun Fu doubted Sun Quan could hold the south while Quan was away at Dongye, so he wrote to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 行人以告，权乃还，伪若不知，与张昭共见辅，权谓辅曰：“兄厌乐邪，何为呼他人？

translations.literal: The traveler reported it—Quan thereupon returned—feigning not to know—together with Zhang Zhao jointly saw Fu—Quan said to Fu—"Elder brother weary and displeased—why summon others?
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan learned, he rushed back, feigned ignorance, and with Zhang Zhao confronted Sun Fu: "Brother, are you weary of me—why call in outsiders?"

sentences.zh: ”辅云无是。

translations.literal: Fu said there was not this.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu denied it.

sentences.zh: 权因投书与昭，昭示辅，辅惭无辞。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon threw the letter to Zhao—Zhao showed Fu—Fu ashamed had no words.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan produced the letter for Zhang Zhao to show him—Sun Fu had no answer.

sentences.zh: 乃悉斩辅亲近，分其部曲，徒辅置东。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon entirely executed Fu's intimates—divided his personal troops—banished Fu relocating east.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan executed Sun Fu's confederates, split his guard, and banished him eastward."

sentences.zh: 數歲卒。

translations.literal: Several years died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 子興、昭、偉、昕，皆歷列位。

translations.literal: Sons Xing, Zhao, Wei, Xin—all held successive ranks.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sun Xing, Zhao, Wei, and Xin all rose through office.

sentences.zh: 孫翊字叔弼，權弟也，驍悍果烈，有兄策風。

translations.literal: Sun Yi, courtesy name Shubi—Quan's younger brother—fierce and fiery—had elder brother Ce's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi, styled Shubi—Sun Quan's brother—was as bold and blunt as Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 太守朱治舉孝廉，司空辟。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Zhu Zhi recommended Filial and Incorrupt—Grand Commandant summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhi recommended him filial and incorrupt; the Grand Commandant summoned him.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：翊名俨，性似策。

translations.literal: The Dianlue states—Yi's given name Yan—nature resembled Ce.
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlue records his birth name as Yan and compares his temper to Sun Ce's.

sentences.zh: 策临卒，张昭等谓策当以兵属俨，而策呼权，佩以印绶。〉

translations.literal: When Ce faced death—Zhang Zhao and others said Ce ought leave the army to Yan—yet Ce called Quan—hanging seals and ribbons on him.
translations.idiomatic: They expected Sun Ce to pass command to Yan; instead Sun Ce hung the seal on Sun Quan."

sentences.zh: 建安八年，以偏將軍領丹楊太守，時年二十。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jian'an—as Lieutenant General holding Grand Administrator of Danyang—at that time twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 203, at twenty, he became lieutenant general and grand administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 後卒為左右邊鴻所殺，鴻亦即誅。

translations.literal: Later finally killed by attendants Bian Hong left and right—Hong thereupon also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His aides Bian Hong murdered him and were executed in turn.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历载翊妻徐节行，宜与妫览等事相次，故列於后孙韶传中。〉

translations.literal: The Wu Calendar carries the conduct of Yi's wife Lady Xu—fit to place following Gui Lan's affair—therefore listed later in Sun Shao's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi moves Lady Xu's story to Sun Shao's chapter after Gui Lan's coup."

sentences.zh: 子松為射聲校尉、都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Son Song was Colonel Who Shoots at Sound and Marquis of Douxiang Village.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Song held Colonel Who Shoots at Sound and the Douxiang village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：松善与人交，轻财好施。

translations.literal: The Wu Records states—Song skilled at associating with people—treating wealth lightly—delighting in giving.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lu praises Sun Song for generosity and easy friendships.

sentences.zh: 镇巴丘，数咨陆逊以得失。

translations.literal: Garrisoned Baqiu—several times consulted Lu Xun on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed at Baqiu he often asked Lu Xun for counsel.

sentences.zh: 尝有小过，逊面责松，松意色不平，逊观其少释，谓曰：“君过听不以某鄙，数见访及，是以承来意进尽言，便变色，何也？

translations.literal: Once had small fault—Xun face rebuked Song—Song expression color uneven—Xun observing him slightly relaxed—said to him—"Lord overhearing did not deem me base—several times visited and reached—therefore receiving your intent advanced exhausting words—then changed color—why?
translations.idiomatic: Once Lu Xun scolded him openly; Sun Song bristled until Lu Xun asked why gratitude turned to anger."

sentences.zh: ”松笑曰：“属亦自忿行事有此，岂有望邪！”〉

translations.literal: Song smiled saying—"Subordinate also self angry conduct had this—how could have expectation!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Song laughed: "I was angry at myself—what blame could I hold?"

sentences.zh: 黃龍三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huanglong died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huanglong 231.

sentences.zh: 蜀丞相諸葛亮與兄瑾書曰："既受東朝厚遇，依依於子弟。

translations.literal: Shu Chancellor Zhuge Liang wrote elder brother Jin saying—"Having received Eastern Court's thick favor—clingingly toward sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang wrote Zhuge Jin: the Wu court had favored his house deeply."

sentences.zh: 又子喬良器，為之惻愴。

translations.literal: Moreover son Qiao fine vessel—for him mournful.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved especially for Zhuge Qiao—Zhuge Jin's gifted son.

sentences.zh: 見其所與亮器物，感用流涕。

translations.literal: Seeing objects he presented Liang—moved used flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing gifts Zhuge Liang had sent Sun Song, he wept.

sentences.zh: "其悼松如此，由亮養子喬咨述故雲。

translations.literal: His mourning Song thus—because Liang's adopted son Qiao consulted narrated therefore cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Song's tie to Zhuge Liang came through adopted son Zhuge Qiao."

sentences.zh: 孫匡字季佐，翊弟也。

translations.literal: Sun Kuang courtesy name Jizuo—Yi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kuang, styled Jizuo, was Sun Yi's brother.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉茂才，未試用，卒。

translations.literal: Recommended Filial and Incorrupt Outstanding Talent—not yet tried in office—died.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended filial and as Outstanding Talent, he died before serving.

sentences.zh: 時年二十餘。

translations.literal: At that time twenty odd years.
translations.idiomatic: He was in his twenties.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：曹休出洞口，吕范率军御之。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states—Cao Xiu emerged at Dongkou—Lu Fan led troops resisting him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan describes Cao Xiu at Dongkou and Lu Fan's defense.

sentences.zh: 时匡为定武中郎将，

translations.literal: At that time Kuang was General of the Household Who Establishes Might
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kuang then held General of the Household Who Establishes Might—

translations.literal: (dispatched)
translations.idiomatic: (ordered to)

sentences.zh: 范令放火，烧损茅芒，以乏军用，范即启送匡还吴。

translations.literal: Fan ordered setting fire—burning damaged thatch—thereby exhausting military supplies—Fan immediately memorialized sending Kuang back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fan had him burn supplies—then impeached him and sent him back to Wu.

sentences.zh: 权别其族为丁氏，禁固终身。

translations.literal: Quan separated his lineage as Ding clan—forbade locked lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan struck the Sun surname from his branch and confined him for life.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案本传曰：“匡未试用卒，时年二十餘。

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi examines this biography states—"Kuang not yet tried died—at that time twenty odd years.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes the main text says Sun Kuang died young without office."

sentences.zh: ”而江表传云吕范在洞口，匡为定武中郎将。

translations.literal: Yet Jiangbiao zhuan says Lu Fan at Dongkou—Kuang was General of the Household Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Jiangbiao zhuan places him at Dongkou as a general.

sentences.zh: 既为定武，非为未试用。

translations.literal: Already being Establishes Might—not being not yet tried.
translations.idiomatic: A titled general can hardly be "never employed."

sentences.zh: 且孙坚以初平二年卒，洞口之役在黄初三年，坚卒至此合三十一年，匡时若尚在，本传不得云卒时年二十餘也。

translations.literal: Moreover Sun Jian died in second year of Chuping—Dongkou campaign in third year of Huangchu—from Jian's death to here altogether thirty-one years—if Kuang at that time still lived—this biography could not say died at twenty odd years.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian died in 191; Dongkou was 222—thirty-one years later—so Kuang could not still be "twenties" if the main text is right.

sentences.zh: 此盖权别生弟朗，江表传误以为匡也。

translations.literal: This cover is Quan's separate younger brother Lang—Jiangbiao zhuan mistakenly thought Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei concludes the Dongkou figure was Sun Lang, not Sun Kuang.

sentences.zh: 朗之名位见三朝录及虞喜志林也。〉

translations.literal: Lang's name and rank appear in Three Courts Records and Yu Xi's Forest of Notes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lang's offices appear in the San chao lu and Yu Xi's Zhilin."

sentences.zh: 子泰，曹氏之甥也，為長水校尉。

translations.literal: Son Tai—Cao clan's nephew—was Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Tai—related to the Caos—served as Colonel of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，從權圍新城，中流矢死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe—following Quan besieging Xincheng—hit by stray arrow died.
translations.idiomatic: He died of an arrow while besieging Xincheng with Sun Quan in Jiahe 234.

sentences.zh: 泰子秀為前將軍、夏口督。

translations.literal: Tai's son Xiu was General Who Guards the Van—Xiakou supervisor.

translations.idiomatic: At Sun Quan's accession he became General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 楷常惶怖，而卒被召，遂將妻子親兵數百人歸晉，晉以為車騎將軍，封丹楊侯。

translations.idiomatic: Eldest Zhu—magistrate of Qu'e.

translations.idiomatic: Next Yi—magistrate of Haiyan.

translations.idiomatic: Both died young.

translations.idiomatic: Sun Shen's son Sun Cheng, styled Xianshi.
